Developer comments: None of these libraries clearly document their threat model! Questions: Does DP protect against attacker with database access? Multiple query results? Side-channel attacks? If attacker compromises library?

In security we need explicit threat models. These libraries assume you understand DP theory and can infer threat model. For practitioners: Dangerous. If you don't understand what DP protects against you might use it incorrectly
Uses numpy.random. Is this cryptographically secure? No! numpy.random is NOT cryptographically secure. It's a PRNG based on Mersenne Twister which is predictable!

If an attacker can predict the noise they can remove it! Example attack: Attacker observes results predicts noise removes noise gets true count. This violates the privacy guarantee! DP libraries MUST use cryptographically secure randomness
OpenDP also uses standard PRNGs not cryptographically secure. Critical Security Issue: All these libraries have weak randomness

Attacker makes multiple queries. Attacker learns composition information. This leaks information! The library doesn't: Track budget consumed Prevent exceeding budget Warn about composition Enforce limits. I can easily violate privacy by accident!

Developer makes mistake with wrong sensitivity. This means noise too small. Privacy guarantee violated! The library doesn't verify sensitivity is correct! It trusts developer. But: Developers make mistakes Sensitivity hard to compute Wrong sensitivity=no privacy
Library should: Compute sensitivity automatically Validate against data Warn if seems wrong
When a DP query runs I need to log: timestamp user query epsilon delta sensitivity result true_result dataset IP. But these libraries don't log anything!
Without audit logs I can't: Investigate breaches Verify compliance Track who queried what Detect anomalous access Prove to auditors what happened
Logs must be: Append-only Cryptographically signed Stored securely Backed up Retained for compliance periods. These libraries provide none of this

How do I verify this actually provides DP? Approach 1 Code Audit: Time-consuming error-prone. Approach 2 Penetration Testing: Can't know found all vulnerabilities. Approach 3 Formal Verification: Only OpenDP claims this but can't verify the verification. As security engineer I need: Independent audits Pentest reports Formal verification CVE database Security advisories
None of these libraries have been independently security audited! This is deal-breaker for security-critical applications

Side-Channel Timing Attacks: Can attacker learn from timing? Memory Access: Can observe patterns? Error Messages: Might leak information about data characteristics dataset size sensitive info. Libraries don't discuss side-channels at all. Libraries don't consider: Timing Memory access Error leakage Cache attacks Other side-channels

Failure Scenario 1: Out of budget - what happens? Failure Scenario 2: Invalid parameters - inconsistent handling. Failure Scenario 3: Data validation failure - silently proceeds! This might violate privacy guarantees!
From security perspective fail securely: If something wrong stop and error Don't silently proceed Don't fall back to non-DP Make failures loud. Libraries often fail silently which is dangerous
